text: 22-year-old male. The patient presents with a 2-day history of fever and altered mentation, reporting fever without chills and rigors. He denies sore throat, abdominal pain, headache, loose stool, burning micturition, or seizures. Has a history of tics and is currently taking haloperidol.

speaker: Patient
text:
My main symptom is Fever and altered mentation. I also have Profuse sweating, Generalized rigidity, Confusion and disorientation, Ability to move all limbs, Normal deep tendon reflexes with bilateral downgoing plantar responses.

speaker: Doctor
text: That is an unusual conclusion given your fever, sweating, rigidity, and confusion, which are classic signs of meningitis or encephalitis. Have you had any severe headache, photophobia, or neck stiffness? REQUEST TEST: Lumbar_Puncture, Brain_MRI.

speaker: Doctor
text: The CSF and MRI results are essentially normal, which makes meningitis or encephalitis unlikely despite the fever and rigidity. Given your confusion and sweating, have you recently taken any antipsychotic medications or suffered from a high fever due to an infection? REQUEST TEST: Electrolyte_Panel, Dopa_Melatonin.

speaker: Doctor
